title: Stage path on touch devices: unit squares become 28x44 bars and capstone diamonds render as skewed slashes
detail: On iPad and iPhone (pointer: coarse) the desk hero's stage path (and every KOS.codeUI stage path) draws each unit square U1..U12 as a 28x44 tall rectangle and each capstone diamond as a 16x44 box rotated 45deg, which reads as a broken diagonal stroke rather than a diamond. Mac (fine pointer) is correct. Reproduce: #/subject/code at ipad/iphone.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-ipad.png, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone.png; eval at iphone: .k-cx-dia offsetWidth 16 x offsetHeight 44 with transform rotate(45deg); .k-cx-sq 28x44. css/base.css:115-119 (coarse min-block-size: var(--hit-coarse) on every button) vs css/views/code.css:132,137 (fixed inline-size/block-size), buttons made at js/core/codeui.js:556,567
rootCause: The global coarse-pointer rule raises min-block-size of every <button> to 44px (invariant 69) but the path's square/diamond buttons only set inline-size/block-size, so height grows and width does not; the diamond is then rotated.
fix: Give .k-cx-sq and .k-cx-dia min-block-size: 0 (they are visual marks; the diamond is tabindex -1) and put the 44px hit area on a transparent ::before or wrapper, or raise width with height for the squares (invariant 69: a round/square control must raise its width too).

title: iPhone desk: Daily 20 and Continue squeezed side by side; the Open-lesson button's label spills out of its pill
detail: At 402px the desk's side column (.k-subj-side) switches to a row, so Daily 20 and Continue are each ~180px wide. The Daily 20 body wraps to five lines, and the 'Open 1.1 Your first program' button is nowrap: its text (153px) overflows the 144px pill on both sides, so the label crosses the button border. Continue is a tall card with its content floating in the middle of ~200px of empty space, and its title wraps.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone-d20.png (dpr 2), /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone.png; eval iphone: [data-ui=code.daily20-lesson] 144x44, scrollWidth 153, white-space nowrap; .k-cx-d20 width 180. css/views/study.css:1074-1076 (side becomes a row of flex:1 1 0 cards), button at js/modules/code.js:221-223
rootCause: The phone/compact rule lays the side column as a row of two equal cards whatever their width; k-btn is nowrap with no max-inline-size or ellipsis, and the label names the lesson in full.
fix: Under 560px stack the two side cards (flex-direction: column) or fold Continue into the Daily 20 card when the Daily 20's job is 'Finish 1.1 first' (they point at the same lesson). Shorten the button to 'Open 1.1' or allow wrapping/ellipsis (.k-fit-btn).

title: Stage path scroller clips the current unit's square and its focus ring at its left edge
detail: On iPhone the first square U1 (state current, with a 2-ring box-shadow) starts exactly at the scroller's left edge (both x=34), so the outer ring and the square's left border are cut off.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone-d20.png; eval iphone: U1 left 34 = scroller left 34. css/views/code.css:134 (ring drawn by box-shadow outside the box)
rootCause: The scroller has no inline padding to hold the box-shadow ring of the first/last item.
fix: Give the path row padding-inline of 2*focus-width (or scroll-padding) so the ring is inside the clip.

title: Desk side column: a real Daily 20 task crushes the Continue card to 41px and clips its 'CONTINUE' label (Mac, iPad landscape)
detail: With a task in the Daily 20 (tier pill, title, three concept chips wrapping to two rows, the why line, Start), the Daily 20 card grows to 239px of the side column's fixed 292px (the hero's height). The Continue card gets 41px while its content needs 62px; overflow: hidden cuts the CONTINUE kicker in half under the Daily 20 card's border. Same at iPad landscape (d20 327 of 459, Continue 121, fits) and worse whenever the why line wraps to three lines. The concept chips (k-cx-cchips) wrap one per row on narrow cards, adding rows.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-prog-mac.png (CONTINUE at y~396 cut); eval mac: .k-cx-d20 239px tall, [data-ui=study.continue] clientHeight 41 vs scrollHeight 62; side 292 = hero 292. css/views/study.css:50 (.k-subj-side > :first-child flex: 1 1 auto), :54 (contain: size), :55 (> * { min-block-size: 0; overflow: hidden }); js/modules/code.js:124, 228-234, 51-55
rootCause: The side column is size-contained to the hero's height and its children may shrink to zero with overflow hidden; the Daily 20 card (first child, flex 1 1 auto) takes what it needs, so the second card is what gives way and is clipped rather than the layout growing.
fix: Give the Continue card flex: 0 0 auto (never shrink below its content) and let the Daily 20 card scroll/clip instead, or drop size containment when the content is taller than the hero; render concept chips as one non-wrapping scroller or limit to two chips + '+1'.

title: Subject analytics card stretches its eight tiles over the Retrieval-due list's height, leaving ~120px gaps between rows
detail: On the Code desk the analytics card (k-sa) is in a row with Retrieval due. With 4+ due skills the row is 412px tall and the grid (flex 1 1 0, grid-auto-rows 1fr, tiles justify-content center) spreads two rows of figures across it: Mastery/Lessons at y~560, Skills proven/Tasks passed at y~740, mostly empty dark card between. On iPad portrait (empty account) the 8 tiles stack 2 per row over ~450px, five of them showing only a dash. Conversely with nothing due the Retrieval-due card is a 250px card holding one sentence.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-prog-mac.png, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-ipad.png, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-mac.png; eval mac: .k-sa 412px tall = retrieval-due 412px. css/views/study.css:77-78
rootCause: grid-auto-rows: 1fr with flex: 1 1 0 makes the tile rows absorb whatever height the neighbouring card imposes; tiles centre their content vertically.
fix: Size the grid to its content (grid-auto-rows: auto, align-content: start) and let the Retrieval-due list cap/scroll, or put the shorter column on sticky ride-along (the Reports pack rule). On narrow widths use 4 columns of compact tiles or hide zero/dash tiles (invariant 77).

title: Continue keeps pointing at 1.1 after the learner has worked through 22 lessons
detail: KOS.code.stats().current is the first core lesson whose status is not 'done'. Completed needs all four checks, and the fourth (a retrieval passed) cannot be earned until the card's first review comes due days later. So after reading every page, running every listing and passing every task in lessons 1.1-3.5 (and starting 3.6), the desk's Continue card still says '1.1 Your first program' at 75%, and the hero's current unit ring stays on U1. The learner's real place (3.6) is nowhere on the desk.
evidence: eval after marking pages/listings/tasks for 22 lessons: stats().current.ref = '1.1', evidence('1.1').checks = [true,true,true,false]; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/desk-prog-mac.png (Continue 1.1). js/core/code.js:870 (current = first not done), js/modules/code.js:250-262
rootCause: 'Where to continue' is derived from completion (which includes a time-gated retrieval) instead of coverage (KOS.code.studied) or the last lesson touched.
fix: Continue at the first lesson not yet studied (KOS.code.studied false), or the most recently touched unfinished lesson; leave pending retrievals to the Retrieval card.

title: Task Run can only feed ONE line of input: a correct answer to any multi-line task crashes with ArgumentNullException
detail: The task page's STDIN box is a single-line <input type=text>, prefilled with only the first line of the first example (split('\n')[0]). 158 of 258 tasks have multi-line example input. Pressing Run with the reference answer to 2.9 Guessing game (example input 42/50/30/42) gives 'Runtime exception ArgumentNullException line 5 Value cannot be null', because the second Console.ReadLine() returns null. A learner can never try their program on the example before Check, and the error points at correct code, which teaches the wrong lesson.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/task-run-multiline-mac.png; eval: set editor to KOS.code.task('2.9-guess').answer, click Run -> output 'ArgumentNullException line 5'; Object.values(KOS_CODE.TASKS) with multi-line examples[0].stdin = 158. js/modules/code.js:633-635 (input type text, split first line), :694 (stdin: stdin.value)
rootCause: Run's input was built as a one-line text field and deliberately truncates the example to its first line; an <input> cannot hold newlines.
fix: Use an auto-growing <textarea> (rows = example line count) prefilled with the whole first example stdin; keep Ctrl+Enter to run. Optionally a menu to load example N.

title: Retrieval's 'Next reviews will ask…' dates come from a hard-coded SM-2 formula and contradict the real FSRS schedule
detail: Under a card the page projects its next three reviews as 'in 3 days / in 11 days / in 31 days', computed with ivl*2.5 (SM-2). Answering the card first try (graded Easy by FSRS) shows 'Proven · Easy · next in 8 days' directly above a table still saying 'in 3 days'. Since 20 October every card is scheduled by KOS.fsrs (invariant 111); the projection is invented and never matches. The page subtitle also keeps '6 due today' after the tab count dropped to 5.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/retrieval-after-check-mac.png (next in 8 days vs table in 3 days); js/modules/code.js:1013-1020 (var ivl = Math.max(3, row.ivl||2), ef = 2.5 … ivl*ef)
rootCause: The projection predates the FSRS switch and was not moved to KOS.fsrs; it is not redrawn after a rating.
fix: Project with KOS.fsrs (Good each time from the card's current s/d with KOS.srs.weights() and the retention) or drop the dates and keep only the variation list; redraw after finish().

title: Capstone step bar: steps 2-6 are 26x40 targets on iPhone and every step is 40px tall on iPad
detail: The capstone's six-step bar (Closed-book quiz, Brief & build, Rubric, Kurenai review, Write-up, Result) collapses the inactive steps to number circles on iPhone: each button is 26x40, under the 44px touch minimum in both directions, and the circles sit 4px apart. On iPad every step is 40px tall (75x40 for inactive ones).
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/capstone-C1-iphone.png; DOM measurement iphone: k-cx-step 26x40 (x5), ipad 75x40. css/views/code.css:505 (.k-cx-step min-block-size: var(--sp-40)) — a class rule that beats the zero-specificity coarse rule in css/base.css:115-119

title: After a task passes the page offers no next step and its clock keeps running
detail: Passing 2.9 Guessing game (4 of 4, +26 XP) leaves the page as it was: no 'Next task', 'Back to the desk' or 'Next in the Daily 20' action beside the reward line, so the only way on is the breadcrumb. The task clock in the header keeps counting (00:47 → 00:50 three seconds later) after every test passed.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/code-space/task-checked-mac.png; eval: header time 00:47 then 00:50 after pass
rootCause: The pass handler writes the reward line but does not stop the task timer or render a forward action.
fix: On a proven pass stop the clock (show the time taken) and add a primary 'Next' (the next task of the lesson, or back to the Daily 20/desk).

title: Daily 20 marked Done still says 'you haven't proven Input loops in code yet'
detail: After the Daily 20 task passes, the desk card shows '✓ Done today · +26 XP' under the unchanged why line 'You studied 2.9 and haven't proven Input loops in code yet.', which is now false.

rootCause: planDay's why is computed for the morning pick and printed even when done.

title: Concept id collision: 'validation' is defined for T2.17 and for B.8, and B.8's (loaded later) replaces T2.17's, so T2.17 has no concept of its own
detail: js/data/content/code-t2e.js:26 registers concept 'validation' (Validation, lesson T2.17, ObservableValidator) and js/data/content/code-ub.js:38 registers 'validation' (Validation reports, lesson B.8). index.html loads code-t2e.js (line 396) before code-ub.js (line 397) and KOS_CODE.add overwrites by id, so the running app has only B.8's concept: T2.17's skill-map entry, its retrieval card target and the proof from card t2e-nav (code-t2e.js:411, concepts ['navigation','validation']) land on Bridge B's concept instead. Found 5 Nov while cataloguing units for the VN capstone proposal (read in source; not exercised in the browser).
evidence: js/data/content/code-t2e.js:26, :411; js/data/content/code-ub.js:38, :587; index.html:396-397
rootCause: Concept ids are a flat global namespace with no uniqueness check at registration or in smoke75
fix: Rename T2.17's concept (e.g. 'form-validation') keeping any stored proof keys via a one-time rename, and make KOS_CODE.add throw (or smoke75 fail) on a duplicate concept/task/card id

title: Code settings: 'Practice focus' slider is permanently disabled, whatever tracks are started
detail: Settings › Practice focus shows a range input 'Track share of the Daily 20' with the note 'Start a track to mix it in. Core only for now.' The input is created with a literal disabled attribute and value 0, and nothing ever enables it or reads it: starting T1 or T2 lessons (both tracks are fully released) changes nothing. The card promises a control that does not exist (docs/code-plan.md:525 describes a core-only to 50/50 mix). It also contradicts the shipped rule 'Core or Tracks, never both' (kos-code-23).

title: Code settings states the in-app runner's time limit as 2 seconds; the runner actually allows 2.5 s and the watchdog 4 s
detail: The Runner card reads 'Units 1–6 · time limit 2 seconds a run'. KOS.codeRun defaults the interpreter deadline to 2.5 s and terminates the worker at 4 s; a timeout error then says 'Stopped after 4 seconds.' The user sees three different numbers.
evidence: js/modules/code.js:1428 ('time limit 2 seconds a run'); js/core/coderun.js:217 (ms: 2500), :39 (WATCHDOG = 4000), :202/:234 ('Stopped after ' + WATCHDOG/1000)
fix: Derive the label from the same constant the runner uses (export it from KOS.codeRun).
rootCause: Literal copy not tied to the runner constants

title: 'See the answer?' says only today's first pass loses its reward; in fact the task never pays again
detail: The confirm reads 'You can still finish it, but today's first pass will pay no reward.' The rule in KOS.code.quote is permanent: once seen with no earlier pass (seen && !passAt), every later pass, on any day, returns 'answer opened' and passAt is never set by a seen pass. A learner who opens the answer expecting to earn the task tomorrow never can. The behaviour matches invariant 106; the wording does not.
evidence: Reproduced on #/code/task/1.1-box: confirm, pass → 'No reward · you opened the answer at 10:37', taskState passAt null; js/core/code.js:324 (no day check), :340-356 (seen pass never sets passAt); dialog text js/modules/code.js:875-876; shots/code-space/b4-seeanswer-mac.png
fix: Say 'this task will no longer pay a reward' (or add a day limit to the rule if that was the intent).
rootCause: Dialog copy out of step with quote()

title: SQL tasks: a slow first SQLite load fails a correct answer as an infinite loop, and the kill makes every retry cold again
detail: On a fresh page, pressing Check on T1.2-recent with the task's own answer took 12 s and reported 'Case 1 · 4000 ms · ✗ Did not finish · Stopped after 2 seconds in case 1 · Did not finish — is there a loop whose condition never becomes false? · Usually because: a loop whose condition never becomes false' — C# loop advice for a one-line SELECT. KOS.codeRun.run({lang:'sql', src:'SELECT 1;'}) right after a reload timed out (13.9 s) and so did the next call (10.4 s): sqlRun's watchdog calls sqlKill(), which sets sqlw = null, so the following run is 'fresh' again and pays the whole SQLite load once more. Only when a load happens to finish inside the 8 s window does SQL work (a later Check passed and paid). In this audit harness the raw sql-worker took 16 s to answer its first query (query itself 4.08 s), so the harness CPU was slow — but the logic means a slow device (an iPad on battery, a phone) can stay stuck failing every SQL task, and the message blames the learner's code. The timeout figures are also wrong: the card hard-codes '2 seconds' while the wait was 4 s (warm) or 8 s (cold).
evidence: eval: Check on #/code/task/T1.2-recent after reload → tests pane text quoted above (12339 ms); eval: two consecutive KOS.codeRun.run SQL calls → both {code:'TIMEOUT', msg:'Stopped after 4 seconds.'}; raw new Worker('js/labs/sql-worker.js') → 16295 ms, res.ms 4080. Code: js/core/coderun.js:199-203 (timeout → sqlKill → next run fresh), :174-177; js/core/codeui.js:256-257 (hard-coded '2 seconds' and loop advice for every timeout); js/data/code.js:424
fix: Separate loading from running: post a warm-up message and wait for a 'ready' reply before starting the per-run watchdog (or show 'Loading SQLite…' while it loads); on a timeout keep the loaded worker when the run never started; make the timeout card language-aware (no loop advice for SQL) and print the real limit.
rootCause: Watchdog covers worker boot + run together and kills the booted worker; error copy assumes C#

title: SQL task examples: the expected result table wraps mid-row in a half-width column beside an empty '(none)' input
detail: On every SQL task (T1A) the Examples block keeps the C# two-column layout: INPUT always '(none)' takes half the width and the OUTPUT text table (pipes and dashes) is squeezed into the other half with white-space: pre-wrap, so 'with_vat', the dashed rule and every value wrap onto extra lines and the columns no longer line up ('Coffee | 2.2 |' then '2.64' on the next line). The expected answer — the one thing the learner must match — is unreadable. The task page also shows a STDIN field and 'Run tries your code with the input above' though SQL reads no input.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-sqltask-mac.png (#/code/task/T1.3-vat, mac 1470x832); css/views/code.css:323 (two equal columns), :327 (pre-wrap); js/modules/code.js:823-826 (always Input + Output), :633-635 (stdin always made)
fix: For lang sql (and any example with no stdin) drop the Input column and give the output the full width with white-space: pre and its own horizontal scroller; hide the STDIN row when the runner is sql.
rootCause: Task view assumes a console program with stdin

title: Error and runtime cards: the heading ('✗ Compile error', '◇ The in-app runner can't run this') is near-black on a dark card
detail: Every Code error card's first line — the kind of error, the most important word on it — is drawn in --alarm-ink, oklch(0.16 0.02 22), a near-black meant for text ON a red fill. In Graphite the card's wash is oklch(0.30 …) (compile error) or a 12% sky wash (runtime card), so the heading has roughly 1.5:1 contrast and reads as a smudge; only the red CS code beside it is visible. Affects compile, runtime, timeout and SQL errors in tasks, listings, retrieval and capstones, and the 'Get the full runtime' card.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-compile-error-mac.png, shots/code-space/b4-runtime-offer-mac.png; eval: .k-cx-err-head color oklch(0.16 0.02 22) on bg oklch(0.3012 0.044 290.7) / oklch(0.815 0.095 224 / 0.12); css/views/code.css:79 (color: var(--alarm-ink)); css/tokens.css:1276
fix: Use --alarm (or --text with the ✗ in --alarm) for the head on the wash; give the runtime card its own --code/--text head colour.
devices: all, Graphite and dark shop themes
rootCause: Wrong token: --alarm-ink is ink for an alarm fill, not for a wash

title: Task page: the Problems tab says 0 while it lists the compile error from Run
detail: Run code with a compile error on a task: the status bar reads '1 compile error' and the Problems pane lists 'CS0103 · line 1 …', but the tab count stays 'Problems 0' because counts() only looks at the last Check, not the last Run.
evidence: #/code/task/1.2-types, Run 'Console.WriteLine(x);' → shots/code-space/b4-compile-error-mac.png (tab reads Problems 0); eval Problems pane text 'CS0103 · line 1 · The name 'x' does not exist…'; js/modules/code.js:663-667 (pc = lastCheck && lastCheck.compile)
fix: Count from the last result shown (Run or Check), the same source that fills the pane.
rootCause: Count and pane read different results

title: Runtime card on a task says 'You can still read the listing and its output below' — there is no listing below
detail: The runtime offer card is shared between lesson listings and tasks; on a unit 7+ task page (no runtime yet) Run shows it in the Output pane with the lesson wording 'You can still read the listing and its output below', but a task has no listing or output beneath it.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-runtime-offer-mac.png (#/code/task/7.1-rect); js/core/codeui.js:278
fix: Pass the context (listing | task) and word the closing line for each; on a task say Check needs the runtime too.
rootCause: One string for two contexts

title: Check on a unit 7+ task without the runtime reports 'Compile error RUNTIME'
detail: Before the full runtime is downloaded, Check on #/code/task/7.1-rect fills the Tests pane with the summary 'Compile error RUNTIME' above the runtime offer. Nothing failed to compile; the runtime is missing. The Check button stays enabled although it cannot run anything (notReady tests only the in-app interpreter).
evidence: eval: tests pane text 'Results\nCompile error RUNTIME\n◇ The in-app runner can't run this…'; js/core/codeui.js:394-397 (any check.compile is titled 'Compile error ' + code); js/core/coderun.js:142 (missing runtime returned as an error with code RUNTIME); js/modules/code.js:680-681
fix: Special-case kind 'runtime' in results() (summary 'Needs the full runtime'), or disable Check with a reason until the runtime is ready.
rootCause: Runtime absence travels through the compile-error path

title: iPhone lesson listings: the caption is crushed into a ~110px column beside Run/Reset/Copy and wraps to five lines
detail: A lesson listing's head puts the language tag, the caption (as the 'file' tab, underlined in sky) and the three actions on one non-wrapping flex row. At 402px the actions take ~210px, so a caption such as 'WHERE keeps the rows whose condition is true' wraps word by word into 5 lines, with the sky underline only under the last line, and the one-line listing below is then cut off at the right edge ('SELECT name, price FROM products' runs off). Every C# and SQL listing with a sentence caption is affected; the iPad portrait is tight too.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-topic-T1.2-listing-iphone.png (#/ref/code/T1.2, iphone 402x874); DOM: .k-ced-head > .k-ced-file 'WHERE keeps the rows whose condition is true' + .k-ced-actions; css/views/code.css:20 (display:flex, no wrap), :22 (.k-ced-file as a tab with a bottom border), :25
fix: Let the head wrap (flex-wrap: wrap; caption flex: 1 1 100% under 560px) or move the caption above the head as a figure caption; keep the tab style only for real file names.
rootCause: Editor head designed for a short file name is reused for sentence captions

title: Retrieval due list and skill map truncate the names the learner needs (lesson and card titles end in '…')
detail: On the Mac the Retrieval 'Due' column is fixed at ~260px so card titles truncate ('Where the docs sa…', 'Solutions and pack…') while the stage card beside it has spare width; on iPad landscape the skill map's lesson column is 82px wide inside a 570px row, so every row reads '1.1 Your firs…', '1.3 Variable…', '1.4 Arithmet…'.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-retrieval-seed-mac.png; shots/code-space/b4-skills-seed-ipadl.png; measurements: ELLIP b 'Where the docs say it' 135x20 (mac), ELLIP span.k-cx-skrow-l '1.1 Your first program' 82x18 inside button.k-cx-skrow 570x40 (ipadl)
fix: Let the titles wrap to two lines (line-clamp 2) in the due list; in the skill map give the lesson column a minmax() share or show just the ref with the title as a tooltip/second line.
rootCause: Fixed column widths with nowrap+ellipsis

title: Skill map rows are 40px tall on touch devices
detail: Each skill row (a button opening its lesson) measures 40px high on iPad (both orientations) and iPhone, under the 44px coarse-pointer minimum of invariant 69; the map is a long list tapped with a finger.
evidence: measurement (pointer:coarse): button.k-cx-skrow 570x40 (ipadl), 358x40 (iphone) on #/code/skills
fix: min-block-size: var(--hit) on .k-cx-skrow under (pointer: coarse).
rootCause: Dense row height not raised for coarse pointers

title: Track T2 page: five part cards in a fixed three-column grid leave an empty cell, and the cards stretch to equal heights with blank bottoms
detail: T2 has five parts; .k-cx-parts is repeat(3, 1fr) on the Mac, so the second row holds T2D and T2E and an empty third cell (~380x350 of nothing). Within a row the cards stretch to the tallest, leaving T2A ~70px of blank card under its three lessons. The part head also differs card to card: on T2A/T2C the 'n of m done' sits beside the title, on T2B/T2D/T2E it drops to its own line, so the PROJECT boxes start at different heights across the row. On the same page 'Builds on' reads 'Missing needs link to their units. The track still opens.' — an unclear sentence.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-trackT2-mac.png (#/code/track/T2, mac, seeded); css/views/code.css:470 (repeat(3, minmax(0,1fr))); js/modules/code.js:524 (needs note text)
fix: Let the last row's card(s) span the leftover columns (or use the app's pack/masonry used by Reports), align-items: start, and keep the done count on one line with the title (or always below). Reword the note: 'Not met yet — tap a unit to open it. The track is open anyway.'
rootCause: Fixed column count independent of part count

title: Desk analytics: 'Tasks passed 28 / 30' means passed of tried, unlike every other 'x / y' tile, and its bar reads as nearly finished
detail: In the Subject analytics grid 'Lessons 0 / 131' and 'Capstones 1 / 6' are done of total, but 'Tasks passed 28 / 30' is passed of attempted (258 tasks exist), with a 93% green bar. A learner 11% into the tasks sees an almost-full bar. The label does not say 'of tried'.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-desk-dawn-seed-mac.png (seeded + 27 API passes); js/modules/code.js:147-148 (v: tasksPassed + ' / ' + tasksTried, pct passed/tried); js/core/code.js:876
fix: Show passed of total tasks in released lessons (or label it 'first-try rate' / '28 of 30 tried') so the bar means progress like its neighbours.
rootCause: Ratio semantics differ within one tile grid

title: Unknown Code ids leave the bad URL in the address bar while another page is drawn
detail: #/code/task/nope-1 draws the Code desk, and #/code/capstone/C9, #/code/project/rp-nope, #/code/track/T99 and #/code/bogus draw the Curriculum map, but location.hash keeps the bad route in every case. Invariant 65 says an invalid route is replaced (with Home); here a stale bookmark or a renamed id shows a different page under a URL that names something else, and Back/refresh repeat it. pageTask and codecap.page call KOS.show from inside a render, which draws the new view without rewriting the hash; the map is also the silent default for any unknown page name.
evidence: eval: hashes after navigation unchanged ('#/code/task/nope-1' with h1 'Code'; the others with 'Curriculum map'); js/modules/code.js:594 (KOS.show('subject') inside pageTask), :1579 (return pageMap for any unknown page), :1574-1578; js/modules/codecap.js:44; pageTrack has the same fallback
fix: Resolve ids in the router's decoder (return null for unknown ids so the router replaces the route), or call the router's replace path instead of KOS.show from inside a view.
rootCause: Fallback navigation inside a render bypasses the router's URL handling

title: 'For the computer' shows only the newest four saved tasks and offers no way to reach the rest
detail: Saving six tasks with 'Save for the computer' (the phone's route for tasks after unit 3) leaves the desk card listing four rows, with no count, 'more' link or page; the two oldest saves are unreachable until four newer ones are removed. The card head says only 'saved on the phone'. laterList has no other consumer anywhere in the app.
evidence: eval: KOS.code.laterList().length = 6, desk [data-ui~=code.later] rows = 4, no 'more'; shots/code-space/b4-desk-later-mac.png; js/modules/code.js:353 (items.slice(0, 4)); grep: laterList used only at js/modules/code.js:345
fix: Show the count in the head ('6 saved') and a 'Show all' disclosure, or list all (they are short rows).
rootCause: Hard cap without overflow affordance

title: Retrieval 'Due' listbox: arrow keys move a selection screen readers never hear, and the card does not follow until Enter
detail: The due list is role=listbox with tabindex 0 on the <ol>; its <li role=option> items have no ids and the list sets no aria-activedescendant, so ArrowDown changes aria-selected on item 2 while focus stays on the list and nothing is announced. The stage keeps showing card 1 ('Filter and sort') until Enter, so sighted keyboard users see the highlight and the card disagree. Mouse users click an <li> (not a button).
evidence: eval on #/code/retrieval (8 due): after focus + ArrowDown, activeElement = list, aria-activedescendant null, selected option '2 Write a small class', stage still 'RETRIEVAL · T1A · FILTER AND SORT'; js/modules/code.js:930 (listbox), :940-951 (options without id), :952-956 (keydown only redraws the list)
fix: Give each option an id and set aria-activedescendant on move (or use roving tabindex on buttons), and draw the picked card on arrow as a click does.
rootCause: Custom listbox without the activedescendant contract

title: With 'Phone tasks' switched off, a unit 1–3 task on the phone says 'This one needs a wide editor' and gives no way back
detail: Turning off Settings › Phone › 'Phone tasks · reduced reward (units 1–3)' makes every task fall to the 'Best on a computer' card. The card's reason is fixed: 'This one needs a wide editor. Read it now, write it later.' — untrue for a two-line unit 1 task the phone normally runs, and it does not mention the setting or link to it, so a learner who flipped the switch cannot tell why tasks stopped opening.
evidence: eval at iphone size, ui.phoneTasks=false → #/code/task/1.4-hours shows 'Best on a computer … This one needs a wide editor…'; shots/code-space/b4-phone-off-iphone.png; js/modules/code.js:908 (fixed copy); js/core/code.js:909 (phoneFit false when phoneTasks off)
fix: When the task would fit but the setting is off, say 'Phone tasks are off in Code settings' with a link (or a 'Do it here anyway' button).
rootCause: One reason string for two causes

title: Capstone and Rider project briefs stop at 620px inside an 832px card, leaving a 190px empty strip
detail: On the Mac the 'The brief' card of a capstone's Brief & build step (and the Brief on a Rider project's Overview) caps its prose at max-width 620px while the card is 832px wide, so the text, the solution table and its code chips stop short with a 190px dead strip on the right — the 'no dead space in width' rule. The table in it wraps code names ('planner-data/topics.json') that would fit in the spare width.
evidence: shots/code-space/b4-cap-C4-build-mac.png; shots/code-space/b4-empty-projT1b-mac.png; eval: card 832px, .k-prose.k-cx-capbrief 620px (max-width 620px), gap 190px
fix: Drop the cap inside a card that already sits beside a side column (the card itself is the measure), or narrow the card and widen the milestone column.
rootCause: Reading-width cap applied inside an already-narrow card

title: Search finds Code lessons only under 'Specification' and never finds capstones, Rider projects or tasks
detail: KOS.search.run('LINQ') lists Code lessons in a group labelled 'Specification' (Code has no specification — invariant 24 calls it authored). 'Gradebook' (Capstone 2), 'Reading List' style project titles and task titles return nothing, so the six capstones, thirteen Rider projects and 258 tasks can be reached only by browsing the desk/map.
evidence: eval: search 'LINQ' => 'Specification: 9.6 · Extension methods / 9.8 …'; 'Gradebook' => no groups; js/core/search.js (no Code capstone/project/task source)
fix: Label the group by subject ('Code lessons') and add capstones, projects and tasks (title → #/code/capstone|project|task/<id>) as a Code source.
rootCause: Search indexes the spec tree only
